title: Company-wide policies and processes — Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This page consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard processes for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees, managers, and approvers. Where a policy has operational runbooks or team-specific extensions, links are provided.

Scope and intent:
- Audience: all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors with access to company systems.
- Purpose: reduce operational risk, ensure regulatory/compliance alignment, enable clear approvals and audit trails, and make routine procedures predictable.
- Exceptions: any exception must be recorded in the Risk & Exceptions register and approved by Security and People Ops.

1) Access & permissions
Overview:
Redwood adopts role-based access control (RBAC) with least-privilege principles. All user and service access is provisioned through the Identity Provider (IdP) and tracked in the Access Registry.
Key systems:
- IdP: Okta (primary SSO) — https://okta.redwood.local
- Access registry: AccessDB (internal) — link in the sidebar
- Privileged access: AWS IAM and Vault (HashiCorp Vault) for secrets

Policies and process:
- New hire provisioning: People Ops creates the ticket in the Provisioning queue (Jira: PROV-NEW). Engineering owners add role assignments within 2 business days.
- Privileged access requests (e.g., admin, production DB, Vault unseal): must be submitted using the Privileged Access Request form and approved by the service owner + Security. Approval window is valid for up to 30 days.
- Third-party contractors: must have a sponsor and a documented justification. Access expires automatically at the contract end date.

Approval matrix (summary):
| Resource type | Approver(s) | Duration | Audit cadence |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Non-prod infra | Team lead | 180 days | Quarterly
| Prod infra | Service owner + Security | 30 days | Monthly
| Vault secrets write | Service owner + Security | 7 days | Monthly

Review & recertification:
- Owners receive quarterly recertification reminders. Unattested accounts are disabled after 14 days and removed after 90 days.
- Emergency access is logged and requires retrospective review within 5 business days.

2) Change management
Overview:
All changes to production services, infra, or data stores that could affect availability, integrity, or confidentiality must go through the Change Management process. Non-invasive changes to docs/configs that do not touch production components may follow lightweight approvals.
Change categories:
- Standard (pre-approved, low-risk): routine configuration updates, patching schedule updates.
- Normal (requires review): infra changes, schema changes with no data migration, non-destructive rollouts.
- Major (requires CAB + testing): schema migrations, model rollouts with fallback implications, network changes, major infra upgrades.

Procedure (normal/major changes):
1. Create a Change Request (Jira: CHG-XXX) with the following fields: description, owner, rollback plan, impact assessment, test plan, scheduled window, and SLO impact analysis.
2. Security and Platform review within 48 hours.
3. For Major changes, present to Change Advisory Board (CAB) 3 business days before the window. CAB includes Platform, Security, SRE, Product, and a People Ops representative.
4. Execute in the approved window with live runbook and rollback practice.
5. Post-change review (within 3 business days) documenting metrics and any incidents.

SLO impact thresholds (require escalation):
- >10% increase in 99th percentile latency across requests — immediate hold.
- >2% sustained error-rate increase for 1 hour — immediate rollback/mitigation.

Emergency change path:
- Use the Emergency Change procedure (CHG-EMERG): notify oncall@sre.redwood.com, document the change in the ticket, and schedule a retrospective within 3 business days.

3) Data management & governance
Principles:
- Classify data by sensitivity (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted).
- Apply encryption-at-rest and in-transit for Confidential and Restricted data.
- Minimize copies and use single source of truth (S3 buckets + Lakehouse governance).

Data classification table:
| Classification | Examples | Storage controls | Retention |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Public | Marketing website content | None special | n/a
| Internal | Internal docs, metrics | SSO gate, internal search | 3 years
| Confidential | Customer PII, contract terms | Encrypted S3, limited access | 7 years
| Restricted | Health/regulated data | Encrypted S3 + VPC-only, strict RBAC | As contract requires

Data handling requirements:
- Access requests must state business justification and be time-limited.
- Production data for dev/test: sanitize or use synthetic datasets. See the Data Masking runbook.
- Backups: daily full backups for critical stores, weekly for others. Restore drills annually.

Data breach procedure (summary):
1. Notify Incident Response and Security immediately.
2. Contain access and preserve logs.
3. Triage data scope and affected customers.
4. Notify Legal and People Ops for external communications.
5. Remediate and complete a postmortem within 30 days.

4) Procurement, expenses, and vendor payments
Principles:
- Centralized procurement for hardware, cloud credits, and enterprise software. Decentralized approvals for low-value purchases.
- All purchases above USD 25,000 require Finance + Legal review and an approved Purchase Order (PO).

Procurement flow (summary):
1. Create a Procurement Request in Jira (PROC-XXX) with cost center and justification.
2. Manager approval required for any request > $500.
3. Finance review and PO issuance for > $2,500.
4. Legal review for > $25,000 or contracts with data processing clauses.

Expense policy (high-level):
- Reimbursable expenses must be submitted within 30 days with receipts via Expensify (expense.redwood.com).
- Per-diem and travel class limits: Economy for flights under 5 hours, Premium Economy for 5–8 hours, Business for >8 hours when pre-approved.
- Alcohol on approved client meals is reimbursable up to $50 per meal with justification.

Procurement thresholds (quick table):
| Amount | Approver(s) | Notes |
|---:|---|---|
| <$500 | Manager | Low value, auto-approve in system
| $500–$2,500 | Manager + Finance visibility |
| $2,500–$25,000 | Finance approval + PO | Standard procurement
| >$25,000 | Finance + Legal + Exec sponsor | Contract review required

5) Vendor management
Overview:
Vendors are categorized by impact and data access (Low, Medium, High). High-impact vendors (processing customer data or integrated into production workflows) require a Security Assessment and contract with Data Processing Addendum (DPA).
Vendor lifecycle:
- Selection: complete Vendor Evaluation Checklist and risk assessment.
- Onboarding: create vendor profile in Vendor Registry and assign owner.
- Review: annual security/compliance review for High-impact vendors.
- Offboarding: revoke credentials, delete stored secrets, and record final acceptance.

Vendor evaluation checklist (key items):
- Business justification and expected spend
- Data processed and location
- Compliance certifications (ISO27001, SOC2, GDPR)
- Subprocessor list and audit rights
- Incident response and notification SLA

6) Travel policy (business travel)
Booking and approvals:
- All air travel must be booked through the approved travel partner (Concur).
- Domestic travel: manager approval. International travel: manager + People Ops approval.
- Non-standard travel (personal days adjacent, additional stops): requires manager + People Ops approval.

Safety & insurance:
- Employees traveling internationally must register trips in Concur and ensure emergency contact information is up to date. Travel insurance is provided for business trips by People Ops.

Per diem and lodging guidelines:
- Reasonable hotel (mid-range business hotels) preferred within corporate rate agreements.
- Meals reimbursed up to $75/day in major metros; higher per-diem requires pre-approval.

7) Internal templates and examples
Included templates (copy and adapt from this page):
- Privileged Access Request Form (template):
  - Requestor name:
  - System/service:
  - Justification and business need:
  - Access level required (read/write/admin):
  - Duration (start / end):
  - Approver(s):

- Change Request template (required fields):
  - Change ID, Owner, Summary
  - Risk assessment and rollback plan
  - Test plan and success criteria
  - Scheduled window and communication plan

- Vendor Evaluation checklist (see section above)

- Expense submission checklist:
  1. Upload PDF receipt to Expensify
  2. Tag cost center and project code
  3. Add justification and attendee list (if meal/client expense)
  4. Confirm policy compliance and submit

8) Roles and contact points (owner map)
- People Ops (policy owner, day-to-day): people-ops@redwood.com
- Finance (procurement, invoices): procurement@redwood.com
- Security (access reviews, vendor security assessments): security@redwood.com
- SRE/Platform (change approvals, runbooks): platform@sre.redwood.com
- Legal (contracts and DPAs): legal@redwood.com

9) Compliance, auditability, and KPIs
Metrics tracked quarterly:
- Time-to-provision (new hire access): target <= 48 hours
- Privileged access requests approved within SLA: 95% in 48 hours
- Change success rate (post-review): target >= 99%
- Vendor high-impact assessments completed on time: 100% annually

Audit evidence and retention:
- Access approvals and recertifications retained for 7 years in the AccessDB
- Change requests, runbooks, and postmortems stored in Jira and Confluence for 7 years
- Vendor contracts stored in Contract Repository with DPA attachments

10) Exceptions and escalation
- To request an exception: file a Risk & Exception request and include mitigation, compensating controls, and expiration. Security or Legal will triage and approve.
- Escalation: unresolved approvals or policy disputes escalate to the Head of People Ops for operational issues and to the Chief Security Officer for security-related exceptions.

Appendix A — Quick links and forms
- Privileged Access Request form: /confluence/forms/privileged-access-request
- Procurement request: Jira project PROC
- Vendor Registry: /confluence/vendor-registry
- Expense submission: expense.redwood.com (Expensify)

Appendix B — Change checklist (pre-deployment)
1. Peer review complete and merged
2. Runbook with rollback steps available
3. Load and integration tests green
4. Monitoring dashboards and alerts configured
5. Communication plan to stakeholders

This document is maintained by People Ops and Security. For questions or proposed edits, submit a pull request on this Confluence page or email people-ops@redwood.com.
